what_changed_from_run_1.unchanged: g 3.5, pfo/pfi 1.4375, de 1.25 — CET's defaults in both runs
what_changed_from_run_1.why_this_is_enough: the two terms corrected in defect #10 are (bp/2)*h1*(1/s) and (bp/2)*h0*(1/(2s)). ALL FOUR of bp, h1, h0 and s changed between the runs, so both corrected terms are exercised at genuinely different values. The unchanged parameters (g, pfo, pfi, de) appear only in the (2/g) bracket, which was never in doubt and which the printed expression confirms directly.

prediction_registered_before_reading_cet.method: the report's input block was read first, the module run across the plausible de range and the results printed, and only then was CET's Yp line opened. de = 1.25 was CET's choice.

formula_note: identical to the expression printed on run 1, on different geometry. Two independent printings of the same term structure.

basis: the expression was printed in full by CET on TWO different geometries and is identical both times

residual_limitations_recorded_honestly: g, pfo, pfi and de were CET's defaults in both runs and did not vary. They appear only in terms that were already correct.

the module caps de at s (de = min(geom.de, s)). CET's de = 1.25 is well below s in both runs, so the cap itself is UNTESTED. CET does print 's > pfi', so it evidently carries the same comparison for pfi, but that is inference, not measurement.
both runs used 1 in A325N bolts, Fy 50 ksi plate and Mu 4800 kip-in. Materials and load were not varied — though Yp is purely geometric, so this does not bear on the yield-line parameter.
flag_decision.reversible: this is a judgement that the evidence meets the bar the anchors module was held to (recorded model, matched numbers) and exceeds it by adding a printed formula. If Ahmed disagrees, set VERIFIED['4ES'] = False and the gate closes again.
